draft.title: The trapezoidal rule
card: The trapezoidal rule estimates a definite integral when finding an exact antiderivative is hard or the data is a table. Split the area into strips of equal width h, and treat each strip as a trapezium.
A trapezium has area (sum of parallel sides) ÷ 2 × width. With n strips, h = (b − a) ÷ n, and the function values are y₀, y₁, ..., yₙ.
Adding the strips: area ≈ h/2 × [y₀ + yₙ + 2(y₁ + y₂ + ... + yₙ₋₁)]. The first and last values are used once. Every middle value is used twice.
Example: estimate the integral of x² from 0 to 2 using 2 strips. h = 1, and y₀ = 0, y₁ = 1, y₂ = 4. Area ≈ 1/2 × [0 + 4 + 2×1] = 3.
draft.remember: Use h/2 × [first + last + 2 × (all the middle values)].

a.q: Using the trapezoidal rule with 2 strips, what is the estimate for the integral of x² from 0 to 4?
a.why: Here h = 2, and y₀ = 0, y₁ = 4, y₂ = 16. Area ≈ 2/2 × [0 + 16 + 2×4] = 24, so 20 is wrong: it comes from adding the middle value only once, which gives 1 × [0 + 16 + 4]. The middle value must be doubled, so the answer is 24.
a.clue: Find h first, then double the middle value.

b.q: A function has values 2, 5, 6 and 3 at x = 0, 1, 2 and 3. Using the trapezoidal rule with 3 strips, what is the estimate of the integral from 0 to 3?
b.why: Here h = 1, so area ≈ 1/2 × [2 + 3 + 2×(5 + 6)] = 1/2 × 27 = 13.5. Check by adding trapezia: 3.5 + 5.5 + 4.5 = 13.5. The option 12.5 is wrong because it is not what either method gives.
b.clue: Add the area of each of the three strips and compare.

b.best: none of the options (correct value is 13.5)

problems.detail: No option is correct. With h = 1, the estimate is 1/2 × [2 + 3 + 2×(5 + 6)] = 13.5 (strips 3.5 + 5.5 + 4.5), and 13.5 is not among 12.5, 16, 11 and 25.
The why works out 13.5, which is not an option, and rejects 12.5 without naming any listed option as right. A student cannot select the intended answer.
